If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment swings sharply from positive to negative within 3 days, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment volatility.

If sentiment remains neutral (0.33–0.67) over 7+ days, apply linear smoothing to forecast path in late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.

If sentiment peaks >0.80 and precedes a price spike, add 1–2% upward bias to forecast at 10–15 day horizon to capture sentiment-driven breakout.

If sentiment drops below 0.20 after a price peak, apply 1–2% downward bias to forecast at 10–15 day horizon to reflect sentiment-induced reversal.
